summary: Full backend + frontend testing of the new user-account + event-registration feature. Backend: 11/11 pytest tests pass — /auth/register (RGPD required, min pw, duplicate, success), /auth/login + /auth/me for admin & user, admin-only guards (403 for user on /members and /pages/home; 200 for admin), full event capacity flow (capacity=2, 2 users register, 3rd gets 400 'complet', duplicate 400 'déjà inscrit', DELETE frees a spot, registered_count/spots_left correct on GET /events, my-registrations lists ids, admin sees participant list with name/email/phone). Frontend: /inscription enforces RGPD (register-error shown), successful registration logs in and redirects to /evenements with nav-user-name & nav-logout visible; on /evenements a logged-in user can register (badge event-registered-<id>, unregister button, spots update) and unregister (button reverts); logged-out users see event-login-hint-<id> and clicking S'inscrire redirects to /connexion; admin login redirects to /admin; non-admin user visiting /admin is redirected away to /; admin /admin/events shows event-capacity field and participants-event-<id> button opens participants-modal.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1160 lines and mixes auth, pages, events, gallery, members, analytics, email, upload — consider splitting into routers for maintainability (>700-line threshold).

POST /events/{id}/register sends 2 Resend emails synchronously in the request path (send_email_sync uses requests with 15s timeout each); under email-service latency the endpoint can block up to ~30s. Consider fastapi BackgroundTasks or asyncio.to_thread.

GET /events/my-registrations is declared before POST /events/{event_id}/register (line ~740 vs 745) — order is fine because FastAPI matches literal 'my-registrations' before {event_id}, but any future refactor should keep literal routes first (was verified).
AppContext.register() and login() throw raw axios errors; consumers rely on err.response.data.detail — this is consistent but a small typed helper would DRY the two pages.
Events.jsx doUnregister catch swallows error detail and shows generic 'Erreur.' — could surface backend detail like doRegister does.
